lockup.summary: The company, its directors and officers, and nearly all other holders agreed not to sell shares for 180 days after the prospectus date. All remaining shares can be sold from day 181.

what: It develops long-acting antibody medicines for immune and inflammatory diseases and has no approved products yet.
proceeds: It expects net proceeds of about $152.4 million. About $90.0 million is for its lead drug BBT001 and about $40.0 million for BBT002. The rest is for two early-stage drugs, equipment, working capital and general costs.
risks: The company is young, has no approved products and has a short history, so it is hard to judge its future.
It has lost a lot of money since it started, expects more losses and may never make a profit.
Even if a drug is approved, doctors and patients may not use it, and the market may be smaller than expected.
It faces strong competition, and others may develop or sell rival treatments sooner or more successfully.
Raising more money could dilute current shareholders, limit how the company operates, or force it to give up rights to its drugs.
